- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Encode the images of all waiting multimodal requests with one vision-encoder call right before they are scheduled for prefill, instead of one call per request at admission.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: Closes #8407

## Motivation

Today `add_request` runs the vision encoder once per request, synchronously on the engine loop. When many image requests arrive at once they are encoded one after another: on A100 x2 with Nemotron 3 Nano Omni and 64 concurrent single-image requests, MCore reaches 571 output tok/s against vLLM's 1646 on the same images (Measurements below). A request with several images already hands the encoder its patches concatenated, one `imgs_sizes` row per image, so the images of several requests can be concatenated the same way and the output split back per request. vLLM batches encoder inputs across requests per scheduler step in the same way ([scheduler budget](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db3b0f0fae4bc98492b3863685e541e62bc59576/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1869), [runner batch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db3b0f0fae4bc98492b3863685e541e62bc59576/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L2782)).

## Changes

- `_build_vlm_request` admits a dynamic-resolution image request whose patch tensor is `[P, F]` or `[1, P, F]` without encoding it, and keeps the embedding count its prompt expansion expects (`expected_embedding_count`) on the request as `deferred_image_embedding_count`. Videos, static tiling and cache hits are encoded at admission as before.
- `schedule_waiting_requests` now starts with `_encode_waiting_images`, which encodes all waiting deferred requests together (one `_batched_request_image_encode` call per group of at most `context.max_tokens` embeddings), splits the result per request, validates it, caches it and registers it on the context. Cached images are reused, requests sharing a `media_cache_key` are encoded once, and a shared call that fails (including OOM) or whose output does not match the expected counts falls back to per-request encodes, so a request whose own encode or count is wrong is failed on its own.

Prefill scheduling is the last point before a request enters the context, so encoding there batches everything that arrived since the previous prefill while admission order and abort handling stay unchanged.

## Measurements

Nemotron 3 Nano Omni 30B-A3B (same HF weights for both engines), A100 80GB x2, a distinct 448x448 image per request, 64 output tokens per request (`ignore_eos`), output tokens/s, median of 3 rounds x 3 reps. Every engine sees 280 prompt tokens per request (256 image tokens).

- vLLM 0.32.0, TP2, default V1 settings (CUDA graphs, chunked prefill, prefix caching; no image is repeated, so the encoder cache never hits).
- MCore base = upstream/main `45b68f914`, this PR = `45b68f914` + this commit. Both: Nemotron Omni via Megatron-Bridge (`NemotronOmniInferenceWrapper`), TP2 EP2, `--transformer-impl inference_optimized`, nccl MoE dispatcher, decode CUDA graphs, `--max-tokens 2048`, dynamic-resolution images with the HF preprocessor range (1024 to 13312 patches).

| concurrent requests | vLLM | MCore base | MCore this PR | this PR / base |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 149 | 70 | 71 | 1.01x |
| 8 | 562 | 298 | 374 | 1.26x |
| 32 | 1230 | 488 | 780 | 1.60x |
| 64 | 1646 | 571 | 1019 | 1.78x |

Text-only throughput (128 output tokens) is unchanged: 80/579/1765/2973 on base vs 84/582/1789/3103 tok/s with this PR at conc 1/8/32/64 (vLLM 194/812/2465/4581). Greedy outputs for 8 images sent one at a time and all at once agree for 6/8 images with this PR, 4/8 on base and 5/8 on vLLM; the differences come from bf16 batch composition and exist without this PR as well.

## Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests (`tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine.py`, 22 tests covering admission deferral and its guards, the shared encode and split, cache/dedupe, budget split, failure fallbacks and isolation; two existing admission tests now check the encode after it is deferred)
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests (engine-level behavior covered by unit tests)
- [x] No GPU kernel added or changed
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code
- [x] I have added relevant documentation (docstrings)
- [x] I have run the autoformatter on my PR

## Notes for reviewers

- The group budget counts projected embeddings (what one prefill step can consume), not encoder patches; with pixel shuffle the encoder processes a multiple of that per call. A patch-based cap can be added if this turns out to be too large.
- Each pass encodes every deferred request in the queue, not only the ones this step can admit. The total work is the same as encoding at admission; it is just no longer spread across admissions.
- An image whose encode fails, or whose prompt does not match its images, is no longer rejected inside `add_request`: the request is admitted, and when its encode fails before prefill it is failed through `_handle_failed_request`, so a direct `add_request` caller sees a failed request instead of an exception.

Signed-off-by: Yoonsik Kim <yoonsik.kim90@navercorp.com>
Signed-off-by: Yechan Kim <yechan.78@navercorp.com>
Signed-off-by: Hyungseo Ahn <hyungseo.ahn@navercorp.com>

- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Encode the images of all waiting multimodal requests with one vision-encoder call right before they are scheduled for prefill, instead of one call per request at admission.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: Closes #8407

## Motivation

Today `add_request` runs the vision encoder once per request, synchronously on the engine loop. When many image requests arrive at once they are encoded one after another: on A100 x2 with Nemotron 3 Nano Omni and 64 concurrent single-image requests, MCore reaches 571 output tok/s against vLLM's 1646 on the same images (Measurements below). A request with several images already hands the encoder its patches concatenated, one `imgs_sizes` row per image, so the images of several requests can be concatenated the same way and the output split back per request. vLLM batches encoder inputs across requests per scheduler step in the same way ([scheduler budget](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db3b0f0fae4bc98492b3863685e541e62bc59576/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1869), [runner batch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/db3b0f0fae4bc98492b3863685e541e62bc59576/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L2782)).

## Changes

- `_build_vlm_request` admits a dynamic-resolution image request whose patch tensor is `[P, F]` or `[1, P, F]` without encoding it, and keeps the embedding count its prompt expansion expects (`expected_embedding_count`) on the request as `deferred_image_embedding_count`. Videos, static tiling and cache hits are encoded at admission as before.
- `schedule_waiting_requests` now starts with `_encode_waiting_images`, which encodes all waiting deferred requests together (one `_batched_request_image_encode` call per group of at most `context.max_tokens` embeddings), splits the result per request, validates it, caches it and registers it on the context. Cached images are reused, requests sharing a `media_cache_key` are encoded once, and a shared call that fails (including OOM) or whose output does not match the expected counts falls back to per-request encodes, so a request whose own encode or count is wrong is failed on its own.

Prefill scheduling is the last point before a request enters the context, so encoding there batches everything that arrived since the previous prefill while admission order and abort handling stay unchanged.

## Measurements

Nemotron 3 Nano Omni 30B-A3B (same HF weights for both engines), A100 80GB x2, a distinct 448x448 image per request, 64 output tokens per request (`ignore_eos`), output tokens/s, median of 3 rounds x 3 reps. Every engine sees 280 prompt tokens per request (256 image tokens).

- vLLM 0.32.0, TP2, default V1 settings (CUDA graphs, chunked prefill, prefix caching; no image is repeated, so the encoder cache never hits).
- MCore base = upstream/main `45b68f914`, this PR = `45b68f914` + this commit. Both: Nemotron Omni via Megatron-Bridge (`NemotronOmniInferenceWrapper`), TP2 EP2, `--transformer-impl inference_optimized`, nccl MoE dispatcher, decode CUDA graphs, `--max-tokens 2048`, dynamic-resolution images with the HF preprocessor range (1024 to 13312 patches).

| concurrent requests | vLLM | MCore base | MCore this PR | this PR / base |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 149 | 70 | 71 | 1.01x |
| 8 | 562 | 298 | 374 | 1.26x |
| 32 | 1230 | 488 | 780 | 1.60x |
| 64 | 1646 | 571 | 1019 | 1.78x |

Text-only throughput (128 output tokens) is unchanged: 80/579/1765/2973 on base vs 84/582/1789/3103 tok/s with this PR at conc 1/8/32/64 (vLLM 194/812/2465/4581). Greedy outputs for 8 images sent one at a time and all at once agree for 6/8 images with this PR, 4/8 on base and 5/8 on vLLM; the differences come from bf16 batch composition and exist without this PR as well.

## Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests (`tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine.py`, 22 tests covering admission deferral and its guards, the shared encode and split, cache/dedupe, budget split, failure fallbacks and isolation; two existing admission tests now check the encode after it is deferred)
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests (engine-level behavior covered by unit tests)
- [x] No GPU kernel added or changed
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code
- [x] I have added relevant documentation (docstrings)
- [x] I have run the autoformatter on my PR

## Notes for reviewers

- The group budget counts projected embeddings (what one prefill step can consume), not encoder patches; with pixel shuffle the encoder processes a multiple of that per call. A patch-based cap can be added if this turns out to be too large.
- Each pass encodes every deferred request in the queue, not only the ones this step can admit. The total work is the same as encoding at admission; it is just no longer spread across admissions.
- An image whose encode fails, or whose prompt does not match its images, is no longer rejected inside `add_request`: the request is admitted, and when its encode fails before prefill it is failed through `_handle_failed_request`, so a direct `add_request` caller sees a failed request instead of an exception.

+            return None

+    def _encode_waiting_images(self) -> None:
+        """Encode the images of waiting requests whose admission deferred the encode.
+
+        ``_build_vlm_request`` admits batchable image requests without running the vision
+        encoder. This runs right before waiting requests are scheduled for prefill, so the
+        images of every such request that arrived since the last prefill go through the
+        encoder together: a request with several images already hands
+        ``_forward_vision_encoder`` their patches concatenated with one ``imgs_sizes`` row per
+        image, so the images of several requests are concatenated the same way and the output
+        is split back by each request's embedding count. One call covers at most
+        ``context.max_tokens`` embeddings. Cache hits are filled from the vision cache,
+        requests sharing a ``media_cache_key`` are encoded once, a group whose shared encode
+        fails falls back to per-request encodes, and a request whose encode fails is failed
+        on its own and removed from the waiting queue.
+        """
+        if not self._has_deferred_image_encodes:
+            return
+        deferred = [
+            request
+            for request in (self.get_request(rid) for rid in self.waiting_request_ids)
+            if isinstance(request, DynamicVLMInferenceRequest)
+            and request.deferred_image_embedding_count is not None
+            and request.image_embeddings is None
+        ]
+        if not deferred:
+            self._has_deferred_image_encodes = False
+            return
+        try:
+            self._encode_deferred_requests(deferred)
+        finally:
+            # Anything still waiting without embeddings (after an exception above, or a
+            # request failed further down) is picked up by the next pass.
+            self._has_deferred_image_encodes = any(
+                request.image_embeddings is None and request.request_id in self.waiting_request_ids
+                for request in deferred
+            )
+
+    def _encode_deferred_requests(self, deferred: List[DynamicVLMInferenceRequest]) -> None:
+        """Encode, register or fail the given waiting requests (see _encode_waiting_images)."""
+        encoded: Dict[int, Tensor] = {}
+        failed: Dict[int, Exception] = {}
+        pending: List[Tuple[DynamicVLMInferenceRequest, int]] = []
+        first_request_by_key: Dict[str, int] = {}
+        duplicates: List[Tuple[DynamicVLMInferenceRequest, int]] = []
+        # Requests whose embeddings alias a tensor the cache or another request already
+        # holds; they are registered without inserting into the cache again.
+        aliased_ids = set()
+        for request in deferred:
+            cached = self._get_cached_vision_embedding(request.media_cache_key)
+            if cached is not None:
+                encoded[request.request_id] = cached
+                aliased_ids.add(request.request_id)
+                continue
+            key = request.media_cache_key
+            if key and key in first_request_by_key:
+                duplicates.append((request, first_request_by_key[key]))
+                continue
+            if key:

+            pending.append((request, request.deferred_image_embedding_count))

+        budget = int(self.context.max_tokens)

+        group_total = 0
+        for item in pending:
+            if groups[-1] and group_total + item[1] > budget:
+                groups.append([])
+                group_total = 0
+            groups[-1].append(item)
+            group_total += item[1]

+        for group in groups:
+            if len(group) > 1 and not self._shared_image_encode_disabled:
+                try:
+                    encoded.update(self._encode_image_requests_together(group))
+                    continue
+                except _SharedEncodeLayoutError as error:

+                    # split: stop deferring instead of paying a wasted shared call every step.
+                    self._shared_image_encode_disabled = True
+                    logger.warning(

+                        error,
+                    )

+                    # handled per request below instead of taking the engine down.
+                    logger.warning(

+                        error,
+                    )
+            for request, _ in group:
+                try:
+                    encoded[request.request_id] = self._encode_image_request(request)
+                except Exception as error:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+                    failed[request.request_id] = error
+
+        for request, first_request_id in duplicates:
+            if first_request_id in encoded:
+                encoded[request.request_id] = encoded[first_request_id]
+                aliased_ids.add(request.request_id)
+            elif first_request_id in failed:
+                failed[request.request_id] = failed[first_request_id]
+
+        for request in deferred:
+            embeddings = encoded.get(request.request_id)
+            if embeddings is None or request.request_id in failed:
+                continue

+            self.waiting_request_ids.remove(request_id)
+            self._handle_failed_request(request_id, stage="encode its images before prefill")
+
+    def _encode_image_requests_together(
+        self, group: List[Tuple[DynamicVLMInferenceRequest, int]]
+    ) -> Dict[int, Tensor]:
+        """Run one vision-encoder call over the images of several requests and split it back.
+
+        Args:
+            group: ``(request, embedding_count)`` pairs whose summed count fits the budget.
+
+        Returns:
+            Dict[int, Tensor]: Each request's slice of the encoder output, keyed by request id.
+        """
+        device = torch.cuda.current_device()
+        imgs = [request.imgs.to(device=device) for request, _ in group]
+        ndims = {tensor.ndim for tensor in imgs}
+        if ndims == {2}:
+            patch_dim = 0
+        elif ndims == {3} and all(tensor.shape[0] == 1 for tensor in imgs):
+            patch_dim = 1
+        else:
+            raise _SharedEncodeLayoutError(
+                f"cannot concatenate image tensors of shapes {[tuple(t.shape) for t in imgs]}"
+            )
+        imgs_sizes = torch.cat([request.imgs_sizes.to(device=device) for request, _ in group])
+        counts = [count for _, count in group]
+        total = sum(counts)
+        nvtx_range_push("megatron.inference.multimodal.batched_vision_encoder")
+        try:
+            with torch.inference_mode():
+                embeddings = self.controller.inference_wrapped_model._forward_vision_encoder(
+                    torch.cat(imgs, dim=patch_dim), num_image_tiles=None, imgs_sizes=imgs_sizes
+                )
+        finally:
+            nvtx_range_pop("megatron.inference.multimodal.batched_vision_encoder")
+        if embeddings.ndim >= 1 and embeddings.shape[0] == total:
+            split_dim = 0
+        elif embeddings.ndim >= 2 and embeddings.shape[0] == 1 and embeddings.shape[1] == total:
+            split_dim = 1
+        else:
+            raise _SharedEncodeLayoutError(
+                f"shared vision encode of {len(group)} requests produced shape "
+                f"{tuple(embeddings.shape)}, expected {total} embeddings on a leading dim"
+            )
+        # The slices are views of one tensor, which lives until the last of these requests
+        # finishes. A slice that goes into the vision cache is copied instead: the cache sizes
+        # entries by their storage and keeps them past the group.
+        cache_on = self.vision_embedding_cache_max_bytes > 0
+        return {
+            request.request_id: (piece.clone() if cache_on and request.media_cache_key else piece)
+            for (request, _), piece in zip(group, torch.split(embeddings, counts, dim=split_dim))
+        }
+
+    def _encode_image_request(self, request: DynamicVLMInferenceRequest) -> Tensor:
+        """Run the vision encoder for one request's images (the per-request path)."""
+        device = torch.cuda.current_device()
+        with torch.inference_mode():
+            return self.controller.inference_wrapped_model._forward_vision_encoder(
+                request.imgs.to(device=device),
+                num_image_tiles=None,
+                imgs_sizes=request.imgs_sizes.to(device=device),
+            )
+
+    def _attach_image_embeddings(
+        self, request: DynamicVLMInferenceRequest, embeddings: Tensor, *, cache: bool = True
+    ) -> None:
+        """Validate and register the embeddings of a request whose encode was deferred."""
+        self._register_image_embeddings(
+            request,
+            embeddings,
+            request.image_token_mask,
+            expected_count=request.deferred_image_embedding_count,
+            modality="image",
+            imgs=request.imgs,
+            num_tiles=None,
+            imgs_sizes=request.imgs_sizes,
+            num_frames=None,
+            error_subject=f"Request {request.request_id}",
+            cache=cache,
         )
